sanskrit: nānṛjur nākṛtātmā ca nāvaidyo na ca pāpakṛt snāti tīrtheṣu kauravya na ca vakramatir naraḥ
english: Neither the dishonest, nor the undisciplined self, nor the ignorant, nor the sinful, nor the crooked-minded man, O Kauravya, bathes in the sacred tirthas.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu dharmamatir nityaṃ dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo bhūya eva bhaviṣyasi
english: But you, whose mind is ever set on dharma, who are learned in righteousness and true to your vows, shall be freed from all sins and become even greater.

sanskrit: yathā bhagīratho rājā rājānaś ca gayādayaḥ yathā yayātiḥ kaunteya tathā tvam api pāṇḍava
english: Just as King Bhagīratha and kings like Gaya, and just as Yayāti, O son of Kuntī, so too shall you, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na harṣāt saṃprapaśyāmi vākyasyāsyottaraṃ kva cit smared dhi devarājo yaṃ kiṃ nāmābhyadhikaṃ tataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In my joy I cannot find words to reply. Who is greater than the one whom the king of gods himself remembers? What name surpasses that?

sanskrit: bhavatā saṃgamo yasya bhrātā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ vāsavaḥ smarate yasya ko nāmābhyadhikas tataḥ
english: Who is greater than he who has your company, whose brother is Dhanañjaya, and whom Vāsava himself remembers?

sanskrit: yac ca māṃ bhagavān āha tīrthānāṃ darśanaṃ prati dhaumyasya vacanād eṣā buddhiḥ pūrvaṃ kṛtaiva me
english: And as for what you, reverend sir, have told me regarding the visitation of tirthas — this resolve was already made by me earlier, upon the counsel of Dhaumya.

sanskrit: tad yadā manyase brahman gamanaṃ tīrthadarśane tadaiva gantāsmi dṛḍham eṣa me niścayaḥ paraḥ
english: Therefore, when you think it right, O brahmin, for the journey to visit the tirthas, I shall go then and there — this is my firm and highest resolve.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gamane kṛtabuddhiṃ taṃ pāṇḍavaṃ lomaśo 'bravīt laghur bhava mahārāja laghuḥ svairaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To that Pāṇḍava who had resolved to set out, Lomaśa said: Travel light, O great king; traveling light, you shall go freely.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bikṣābhujo nivartantāṃ brāhmaṇā yatayaś ca ye ye cāpy anugatāḥ paurā rājabhaktipuraskṛtāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Let the brahmins who live by begging and the ascetics turn back, and likewise those citizens who have followed out of devotion to the king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahārājam abhigacchantu caiva te sa dāsyati yathākālam ucitā yasya yā bhṛtiḥ
english: Let them go to the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he shall give in due time to each person the appropriate support.

sanskrit: sa ced yathocitāṃ vṛttiṃ na dadyān manujeśvaraḥ asmatpriyahitārthāya pāñcālyo vaḥ pradāsyati
english: And if that lord of men does not give the fitting livelihood, then for our sake and your welfare, the king of Pāñcāla shall provide for you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato bhūyiṣṭhaśaḥ paurā gurubhārasamāhitāḥ viprāś ca yatayo yuktā jagmur nāgapuraṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thereupon most of the citizens, weighed down with heavy burdens, and the brahmins and devoted ascetics went toward Nāgapura.

sanskrit: tān sarvān dharmarājasya premṇā rājāmbikāsutaḥ pratijagrāha vidhivad dhanaiś ca samatarpayat
english: The king, son of Ambikā, received all of them with love, as befitting the Dharma-king, and satisfied them with gifts of wealth according to proper rites.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntīsuto rājā laghubhir brāhmaṇaiḥ saha lomaśena ca suprītas trirātraṃ kāmyake 'vasat
english: Then the king, son of Kuntī, greatly pleased, dwelt for three nights at Kāmyaka with a reduced company of brahmins and with Lomaśa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prayāntaṃ kaunteyaṃ brāhmaṇā vanavāsinaḥ abhigamya tadā rājann idaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, the brahmins dwelling in the forest approached the son of Kuntī as he was about to depart and spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: rājaṃs tīrthāni gantāsi puṇyāni bhrātṛbhiḥ saha devarṣiṇā ca sahito lomaśena mahātmanā
english: O king, you are going to the holy tirthas together with your brothers, accompanied by the divine sage, the great-souled Lomaśa.

sanskrit: asmān api mahārāja netum arhasi pāṇḍava asmābhir hi na śakyāni tvad ṛte tāni kaurava
english: You should take us along as well, O great king, O Pāṇḍava; for without you, O Kaurava, we are unable to reach those tirthas.

sanskrit: śvāpadair upasṛṣṭāni durgāṇi viṣamāṇi ca agamyāni narair alpais tīrthāni manujeśvara
english: The tirthas are beset by wild beasts, are difficult and treacherous, and impassable for men of small number, O lord of men.

sanskrit: bhavanto bhrātaraḥ śūrā dhanurdharavarāḥ sadā bhavadbhiḥ pālitāḥ śūrair gacchema vayam apy uta
english: You and your brothers are heroes, the foremost bearers of the bow; protected always by you brave ones, we too would journey there.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād dhi vayaṃ prāpnuyāma phalaṃ śubham tīrthānāṃ pṛthivīpāla vratānāṃ ca viśāṃ pate
english: By your grace we shall attain the auspicious fruit of the tirthas and of our vows, O protector of the earth, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tava vīryaparitrātāḥ śuddhās tīrthapariplutāḥ bhavema dhūtapāpmānas tīrthasaṃdarśanān nṛpa
english: Protected by your valor, purified by immersion in the tirthas, we would become cleansed of sins through the sight of the holy places, O king.

sanskrit: bhavān api narendrasya kārtavīryasya bhārata aṣṭakasya ca rājarṣer lomapādasya caiva ha
english: And you, O Bhārata, shall also attain the worlds of King Kārtavīrya, of the royal sage Aṣṭaka, and of Lomapada —

sanskrit: bharatasya ca vīrasya sārvabhaumasya pārthiva dhruvaṃ prāpsyasi duṣprāpāṃl lokāṃs tīrthapariplutaḥ
english: — and of the heroic universal sovereign Bharata, O king; you will surely attain worlds difficult to reach, by bathing at the tirthas.

sanskrit: prabhāsādīni tīrthāni mahendrādīṃś ca parvatān gaṅgādyāḥ saritaś caiva plakṣādīṃś ca vanaspatīn tvayā saha mahīpāla draṣṭum icchāmahe vayam
english: The tirthas beginning with Prabhāsa, the mountains beginning with Mahendra, the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, and the sacred trees beginning with the Plaksha — we wish to see all these together with you, O protector of the earth.

sanskrit: yadi te brāhmaṇeṣv asti kā cit prītir janādhipa kuru kṣipraṃ vaco 'smākaṃ tataḥ śreyo 'bhipatsyase
english: If you have any affection for brahmins, O lord of the people, heed our words quickly, and you shall attain the highest good.

sanskrit: tīrthāni hi mahābāho tapovighnakaraiḥ sadā anukīrṇāni rakṣobhis tebhyo nas trātum arhasi
english: For the tirthas, O mighty-armed one, are always thronged with rakshasas that obstruct austerities; you must protect us from them.

sanskrit: tīrthāny uktāni dhaumyena nāradena ca dhīmatā yāny uvāca ca devarṣir lomaśaḥ sumahātapāḥ
english: The tirthas spoken of by Dhaumya and by the wise Nārada, and those spoken of by the divine sage Lomaśa of great austerity —

sanskrit: vidhivat tāni sarvāṇi paryaṭasva narādhipa dhūtapāpmā sahāsmābhis tīrthābhigamanāt pūtā darśanāc ca mahātmanām lomaśena ca pālitaḥ
english: — visit all of those duly, O lord of men; purified of sins, with us, protected by Lomaśa and purified by the visit to tirthas and by the sight of great souls.

sanskrit: sa tathā pūjyamānas tair harṣād aśrupariplutaḥ bhīmasenādibhir vīrair bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ bāḍham ity abravīt sarvāṃs tān ṛṣīn pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ
english: Thus honored by them, his eyes filled with tears of joy, surrounded by his brothers — the heroes led by Bhīmasena — the bull of the Pāṇḍavas said to all those sages: "So be it."

sanskrit: lomaśaṃ samanujñāpya dhaumyaṃ caiva purohitam tataḥ sa pāṇḍavaśreṣṭho bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vaśī draupadyā cānavadyāṅgyā gamanāya mano dadhe
english: Having taken leave of Lomaśa and of Dhaumya the family priest, that foremost of Pāṇḍavas, self-controlled, together with his brothers and with the flawless-limbed Draupadī, set his mind on departure.

sanskrit: atha vyāso mahābhāgas tathā nāradaparvatau kāmyake pāṇḍavaṃ draṣṭuṃ samājagmur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Then the greatly blessed Vyāsa, and likewise Nārada and Parvata, those wise ones, came to Kāmyaka to see the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā pūjāṃ cakre yathāvidhi satkṛtās te mahābhāgā yudhiṣṭhiram athābruvan
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira paid homage to them according to the proper rites; and those greatly blessed ones, duly honored, then spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira yamau bhīma manasā kurutārjavam manasā kṛtaśaucā vai śuddhās tīrthāni gacchata
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, the twins, Bhīma — maintain purity of mind; with the mind made clean and pure, go to the tirthas."

sanskrit: śarīraniyamaṃ hy āhur brāhmaṇā mānuṣaṃ vratam manoviśuddhāṃ buddhiṃ ca daivam āhur vrataṃ dvijāḥ
english: For the brahmins declare bodily discipline to be the human vow, while the twice-born call purity of mind and intellect the divine vow.

sanskrit: mano hy aduṣṭaṃ śūrāṇāṃ paryāptaṃ vai narādhipa maitrīṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya śuddhās tīrthāni gacchata
english: An undefiled mind is indeed sufficient for heroes, O lord of men; abiding in a spirit of friendliness, go pure to the tirthas.

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ mānasaiḥ śuddhāḥ śarīraniyamavrataiḥ daivaṃ vrataṃ samāsthāya yathoktaṃ phalam āpsyatha
english: You who are pure in mind, observing the vow of bodily discipline, and embracing the divine vow, shall obtain the fruit as prescribed.

sanskrit: te tatheti pratijñāya kṛṣṇayā saha pāṇḍavāḥ kṛtasvastyayanāḥ sarve munibhir divyamānuṣaiḥ
english: Having pledged "So be it," the Pāṇḍavas together with Kṛṣṇa were blessed with benedictions by all the sages both divine and human.

sanskrit: lomaśasyopasaṃgṛhya pādau dvaipāyanasya ca nāradasya ca rājendra devarṣeḥ parvatasya ca
english: Grasping the feet of Lomaśa, of Dvaipāyana, of Nārada, O king of kings, and of the divine sage Parvata —

sanskrit: dhaumyena sahitā vīrās tathānyair vanavāsibhiḥ mārgaśīrṣyām atītāyāṃ puṣyeṇa prayayus tataḥ
english: — the heroes, together with Dhaumya and other forest dwellers, then set out when the month of Mārgaśīrṣa had passed, under the Puṣya asterism.

sanskrit: kaṭhināni samādāya cīrājinajaṭādharāḥ abhedyaiḥ kavacair yuktās tīrthāny anvacaraṃs tadā
english: Taking up their hard bows, clad in bark garments and deer skins, with matted locks, wearing impenetrable armor, they then traversed the tirthas.

sanskrit: indrasenādibhir bhṛtyaiḥ rathaiḥ paricaturdaśaiḥ mahānasavyāpṛtaiś ca tathānyaiḥ paricārakaiḥ
english: With servants headed by Indrasena, with fourteen chariots, those engaged in kitchen duties, and other attendants —

sanskrit: sāyudhā baddhaniṣṭriṃśās tūṇavantaḥ samārgaṇāḥ prāṅmukhāḥ prayayur vīrāḥ pāṇḍavā janamejaya
english: — armed with weapons, swords girded at their sides, bearing quivers and arrows, facing east, those heroes the Pāṇḍavas set forth, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na vai nirguṇam ātmānaṃ manye devarṣisattama tathāsmi duḥkhasaṃtapto yathā nānyo mahīpatiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I do not consider myself to be without virtue, O best of divine sages; yet I am tormented by sorrow as no other king on earth is.

sanskrit: parāṃś ca nirguṇān manye na ca dharmaratān api te ca lomaśa loke 'sminn ṛdhyante kena ketunā
english: And I see others devoid of virtue and not devoted to dharma — yet they, O Lomaśa, prosper in this world; by what standard does this happen?

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca nātra duḥkhaṃ tvayā rājan kāryaṃ pārtha kathaṃ cana yad adharmeṇa vardherann adharmarucayo janāḥ
english: Lomaśa said: You must not grieve over this at all, O king, O Pārtha — that those who delight in adharma flourish through unrighteousness.

sanskrit: vardhaty adharmeṇa naras tato bhadrāṇi paśyati tataḥ sapatnāñ jayati samūlas tu vinaśyati
english: A man may prosper through unrighteousness, then see good fortune, then conquer his enemies — but he is destroyed root and all.

sanskrit: mayā hi dṛṣṭā daiteyā dānavāś ca mahīpate vardhamānā hy adharmeṇa kṣayaṃ copagatāḥ punaḥ
english: For I have seen the Daityas and Dānavas, O lord of the earth, thriving through unrighteousness and then coming to ruin again.

sanskrit: purā devayuge caiva dṛṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ mayā vibho arocayan surā dharmaṃ dharmaṃ tatyajire 'surāḥ
english: Long ago, even in the age of the gods, I witnessed everything, O lord: the gods embraced dharma, while the asuras abandoned dharma.

sanskrit: tīrthāni devā viviśur nāviśan bhāratāsurāḥ tān adharmakṛto darpaḥ pūrvam eva samāviśat
english: The gods entered the sacred tirthas; the asuras, O Bhārata, did not enter them. Those who practiced adharma were first overtaken by arrogance.

sanskrit: darpān mānaḥ samabhavan mānāt krodho vyajāyata krodhād ahrīs tato 'lajjā vṛttaṃ teṣāṃ tato 'naśat
english: From arrogance came pride; from pride, anger arose; from anger came shamelessness; then disgrace; and thus their conduct perished.

sanskrit: tān alajjān gatahrīkān hīnavṛttān vṛthāvratān kṣamā lakṣmīś ca dharmaś ca nacirāt prajahus tataḥ lakṣmīs tu devān agamad alakṣmīr asurān nṛpa
english: From those who had lost shame, shed modesty, fallen in conduct, and broken their vows — forbearance, Lakṣmī, and dharma soon departed; Lakṣmī went to the gods and ill-fortune came to the asuras, O king.

sanskrit: tān alakṣmīsamāviṣṭān darpopahatacetasaḥ daiteyān dānavāṃś caiva kalir apy āviśat tataḥ
english: Those Daityas and Dānavas, thus overcome by ill-fortune and their minds shattered by arrogance, were then also entered by Kali.

sanskrit: tān alakṣmīsamāviṣṭān dānavān kalinā tathā darpābhibhūtān kaunteya kriyāhīnān acetasaḥ
english: Those Dānavas, overcome by ill-fortune and Kali, overwhelmed by arrogance, devoid of ritual acts and bereft of understanding, O son of Kuntī —

sanskrit: mānābhibhūtān acirād vināśaḥ pratyapadyata niryaśasyās tato daityāḥ kṛtsnaśo vilayaṃ gatāḥ
english: — conquered by pride, soon met with destruction; the Daityas, stripped of glory, were utterly annihilated.

sanskrit: devās tu sāgarāṃś caiva saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca abhyagacchan dharmaśīlāḥ puṇyāny āyatanāni ca
english: But the gods, virtuous by nature, resorted to the oceans, rivers, lakes, and sacred dwelling places.

sanskrit: tapobhiḥ kratubhir dānair āśīrvādaiś ca pāṇḍava prajahuḥ sarvapāpāni śreyaś ca pratipedire
english: Through austerities, sacrifices, charity, and receiving blessings, O Pāṇḍava, they cast off all sins and attained the highest good.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi dānavantaś ca kriyāvantaś ca sarvaśaḥ tīrthāny agacchan vibudhās tenāpur bhūtim uttamām
english: Thus the gods, endowed with charity and full of ritual acts in every way, went to the tirthas, and thereby attained the highest prosperity.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api rājendra snātvā tīrtheṣu sānujaḥ punar vetsyasi tāṃ lakṣmīm eṣa panthāḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Likewise, O king of kings, you too, bathing at the tirthas together with your brothers, shall regain that Lakṣmī; this is the eternal path.

sanskrit: yathaiva hi nṛgo rājā śibir auśīnaro yathā bhagīratho vasumanā gayaḥ pūruḥ purūravāḥ
english: Just as King Nṛga, and Śibi the son of Uśīnaras, Bhagīratha, Vasumanas, Gaya, Pūru, Purūravas —

sanskrit: caramāṇās tapo nityaṃ sparśanād ambhasaś ca te tīrthābhigamanāt pūtā darśanāc ca mahātmanām
english: — always practicing austerity, by the touch of the sacred waters, purified by visiting the tirthas and by the sight of great souls —

sanskrit: alabhanta yaśaḥ puṇyaṃ dhanāni ca viśāṃ pate tathā tvam api rājendra labdhāsi vipulāṃ śriyam
english: — they obtained sacred fame and wealth, O lord of men; likewise, you too, O king of kings, shall attain abundant glory.

sanskrit: yathā cekṣvākur acarat saputrajanabāndhavaḥ mucukundo 'tha māndhātā maruttaś ca mahīpatiḥ
english: And as Ikṣvāku wandered with his sons, kinsmen, and relatives; as Mucukunda, Māndhātā, and the king Marutta —

sanskrit: kīrtiṃ puṇyām avindanta yathā devās tapobalāt devarṣayaś ca kārtsnyena tathā tvam api vetsyase
english: — won sacred fame just as the gods did through the power of austerity, and the divine sages entirely; so too shall you obtain the same.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrās tu darpeṇa mohena ca vaśīkṛtāḥ nacirād vinaśiṣyanti daityā iva na saṃśayaḥ
english: But the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, controlled by arrogance and delusion, shall soon be destroyed just like the Daityas — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te tathā sahitā vīrā vasantas tatra tatra ha krameṇa pṛthivīpāla naimiṣāraṇyam āgatāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those heroes, thus united, dwelling here and there in succession, O protector of the earth, arrived at the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: tatas tīrtheṣu puṇyeṣu gomatyāḥ pāṇḍavā nṛpa kṛtābhiṣekāḥ pradadur gāś ca vittaṃ ca bhārata
english: Then at the holy tirthas of the Gomatī, O king, the Pāṇḍavas performed their ritual baths and gave away cows and wealth, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra devān pitṝn viprāṃs tarpayitvā punaḥ punaḥ kanyātīrthe 'śvatīrthe ca gavāṃ tīrthe ca kauravāḥ
english: There, satisfying the gods, ancestors, and brahmins again and again, the Kauravas visited the Kanya-tirtha, the Aśva-tirtha, and the Gava-tirtha.

sanskrit: vālakoṭyāṃ vṛṣaprasthe girāv uṣya ca pāṇḍavāḥ bāhudāyāṃ mahīpāla cakruḥ sarve 'bhiṣecanam
english: At Valakoti, at Vrishaprastha mountain, and at Bahuda, O protector of the earth, all the Pāṇḍavas performed their ablutions.

sanskrit: prayāge devayajane devānāṃ pṛthivīpate ūṣur āplutya gātrāṇi tapaś cātasthur uttamam
english: At Prayāga, the divine sacrificial ground of the gods, O lord of the earth, they dwelt, immersing their limbs, and undertook the highest austerities.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyamunayoś caiva saṃgame satyasaṃgarāḥ vipāpmāno mahātmāno viprebhyaḥ pradadur vasu
english: At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, those great souls true to their vows, freed from sin, gave wealth to the brahmins.

sanskrit: tapasvijanajuṣṭāṃ ca tato vedīṃ prajāpateḥ jagmuḥ pāṇḍusutā rājan brāhmaṇaiḥ saha bhārata
english: Then the sons of Pāṇḍu, O king, O Bhārata, went together with brahmins to the altar of Prajāpati frequented by ascetics.

sanskrit: tatra te nyavasan vīrās tapaś cātasthur uttamam saṃtarpayantaḥ satataṃ vanyena haviṣā dvijān
english: There those heroes dwelt and undertook the highest austerities, constantly satisfying the twice-born with forest offerings.

sanskrit: tato mahīdharaṃ jagmur dharmajñenābhisatkṛtam rājarṣiṇā puṇyakṛtā gayenānupamadyute
english: Then they went to the holy mountain honored by the righteous royal sage Gaya of incomparable splendor who had performed meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: saro gayaśiro yatra puṇyā caiva mahānadī ṛṣijuṣṭaṃ supuṇyaṃ tat tīrthaṃ brahmasarottamam
english: There is the lake called Gayaśiras, the holy great river, the tirtha beloved of the sages — that supremely holy lake of Brahmā.

sanskrit: agastyo bhagavān yatra gato vaivasvataṃ prati uvāsa ca svayaṃ yatra dharmo rājan sanātanaḥ
english: It is where the blessed Agastya went to meet Vaivasvata, and where eternal Dharma himself, O king, abode.

sanskrit: sarvāsāṃ saritāṃ caiva samudbhedo viśāṃ pate yatra saṃnihito nityaṃ mahādevaḥ pinākadhṛk
english: It is the source of all rivers, O lord of men, where Mahādeva who bears the Pināka bow is ever present.

sanskrit: tatra te pāṇḍavā vīrāś cāturmāsyais tadejire ṛṣiyajñena mahatā yatrākṣayavaṭo mahān
english: There the heroic Pāṇḍavas passed the four-month rainy season rites with a great sacrifice in the manner of the sages, where the great imperishable banyan tree stands.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇās tatra śataśaḥ samājagmus tapodhanāḥ cāturmāsyenāyajanta ārṣeṇa vidhinā tadā
english: Brahmins rich in austerity came there in hundreds, and they performed the four-month sacrifice at that time according to the ancient seer-prescribed rites.

sanskrit: tatra vidyātaponityā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ kathāḥ pracakrire puṇyāḥ sadasisthā mahātmanām
english: There brahmins ever devoted to learning and austerity, masters of the Vedas, seated in the assembly, told sacred stories of great souls.

sanskrit: tatra vidyāvratasnātaḥ kaumāraṃ vratam āsthitaḥ śamaṭho 'kathayad rājann āmūrtarayasaṃ gayam
english: There, O king, Shamatha — who had bathed at the completion of his studies and vows and was observing the vow of celibacy from childhood — told of Gaya, son of Amurtarayas.
